gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Expressive and stencil-flat, Warnes tapers its strokes before they touch. Big, short lines are where it earns its place, while Noto Sans Telugu keeps its midline high and its counters open to the outside.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-thai: Warnes draws plain, unshaded lines, stretched wide. It makes a loud display statement, while Noto Sans Thai rounds out inflated, open letters that feel friendly and easy going.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Warnes makes every curve as stout as its straight stems, with spacious, stretched tracking across each line. Noto Sans Tirhuta follows with a tall x-height and wide gaps, reading smooth and open.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-vai: Warnes sets every diagonal as stout as every upright, giving it a stencil-like, stretched and bold presence. Noto Sans Vai forms its words into solid blocks, which is the quality that holds this pairing together.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Stitched, thread-like strokes make Warnes unmistakable. It is built for shouting big headings, whereas Noto Sans Wancho goes hulking and chalky, with a wide gap at the e terminal.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-parkinsans: Parkinsans keeps one stroke thickness everywhere, with wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp when shrunk down small. Warnes handles the stretched, bold heading above it.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-pathway-extreme: Expressive Warnes has no brush-style swell anywhere, just stretched, flat-edged lines that taper out before they touch. Pathway Extreme sits beside it, stubby and open.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-radio-canada: Expressive and bold, Warnes stretches its tapering strokes wide. Radio Canada gives you tall, full c, s and z shapes with a steady line, so paragraphs move along smoothly.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-roboto: Roboto brings generous mouths on its round letters, and Warnes answers with rounded strokes like cut lengths of cord. One handles the loud display work; the other handles the quiet text.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-saira: Saira lets you see through the gap in each s, with rounded letters stretching high toward the top line. Warnes, meanwhile, draws one unmodulated line across every glyph, so a long stretch of text reads smoothly.
